CORRECTED THE BRIEF'S PREMISE (the key finding): the 22/77 fallback that refused brief-28's [62,100)->k384 peel is NOT the inner-G orthogonality ceiling brief-30 targeted. STEP-1 probe: on the mixed512 rankdef/nearrank subset (77 mats, PR EXACTLY 83.16, cleanly disjoint: 264 dense in [48,62), 76 psd in [37,48), 40 spectrum at 110.9) the INNER G orth is ALREADY 1e-4 orthonormal -- brief-30's _lr_ns_reorth on G was verified to do NOTHING (eig/orth bit-identical with/without it). The fallback is driven by the OUTER Vd=Qd@G block orth (||Vd^TVd-I||_1 up to 1.05; split 18 orth-only + 3 both, only 2-3 eig), because the RANGE-FINDER Qd goes rank-deficient at the exact-rank-3n/4=384 boundary (smallest kept sing val ~1e-2 rel -> after power step ~1e-4 -> CholeskyQR2 loses orthonormality on the last cols). FIX (measured, works): NS-reorthonormalize Qd itself (new _LR_QD_NS_ITERS + _lr_qd_ns_scope, scoped to the band): NS-Qd 0->22/77 fb, 2->1/77, 3->0/77. 0 fallbacks CONFIRMED in the real peel path; scope restores the flag cleanly. k pinned at 384 (k352->77/77 eig fail; k400->77/77), power=1 required (power=0->77/77). Alternatives tested: extraCQR on Qd (0/77 but 20.4ms slower), NS on outer Vd (only 12/77), cuSOLVER inner solve on Bk (32ms, WORSE than split-mega's 17.6ms).

WHY IT STILL DOESN'T WIN (the economics, matching the brief's refute condition): the LR-path floor for the 77-mat subset is ~17.6ms (range-finder n*n*k GEMMs 13.0ms with split-mega inner + 4.6ms complement) but the cuSOLVER MARGINAL saved by peeling the 77 (rest 263->186 mats, 74.95->59.77ms) is only 15.19ms -- LESS than the LR floor -> -2.4ms isolated. The split-megakernel IS already the fastest inner solve here (13ms; cuSOLVER-on-Bk is 27.7ms). The subset (77) is just too small for the LR fixed floor to beat cuSOLVER's marginal, which drops off its knee once dense+psd have already removed 340 mats.

STRANGE DATA-DEPENDENT NS CLIFF (a lead I could not fully explain, worth a follow-up): NS-Qd=2 is a SHARP sweet spot -- shape6 139.6ms (STABLE, 6 runs) -- while BOTH NS-Qd=1 AND NS-Qd=3 sit at ~159ms (+20ms). The split-mega kernel time is IDENTICAL at NS=2 and NS=3 (nsys: mega_eigh_med_split avg 7.1ms max 11.46ms stddev 4.17 both), so the 20ms is NOT the megakernel and NOT the ~1ms/iter NS GEMM cost. It appears in eval.py's L2-flushed bench only (t1's warm isolated timing saw just +2.76ms). Likely an allocator/FP32-NS-GEMM interaction at specific iter counts. If this 20ms artifact were eliminated, NS-Qd=3 (0 fallback) would land near NS-Qd=2's 139ms and the band would be within ~7ms of neutral on shape6.
